findings.observation: Read the Engineer's Summary Letter supplementary document, specifically the section on 'Utilities and Stormwater Management' (pages 1-2). The document states: 'The site is in the West Bouldin Creek Watershed, which is classified as an urban watershed by the City of Austin and allows a maximum 80% impervious cover.' This clearly identifies both the watershed location (West Bouldin Creek) and classification (urban watershed).
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires the ESL to identify watershed location and classification. The ESL explicitly states both elements: the site is in 'West Bouldin Creek Watershed' and it is 'classified as an urban watershed.' This matches the requirement exactly. The watershed classification is also confirmed in facts.md, which shows the same information. The ESL provides the required information in a clear, unambiguous manner.
findings.explanation: ESL identifies West Bouldin Creek Watershed as an urban watershed in the Utilities and Stormwater Management section

findings.observation: Used vision tool and semantic search to locate overhead utility lines. Vision analysis of Sheet 8 confirms overhead electric lines are shown with the notation 'EXISTING OVERHEAD UTILITY LINE TO BE REMOVED' and power poles are marked. Sheet 9 (Existing Conditions 2 of 2) shows overhead electric lines marked '-OHE-' along South Lamar Boulevard and Collier Street with existing power poles. Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan) legend defines 'PROPOSED OVERHEAD ELECTRIC LINE' with line type 'OHE'. Vision analysis confirms overhead electric lines marked '--- OHE ---' are shown along Collier Street and Kinney Avenue on Sheet 14.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires overhead utility lines (existing and proposed) to be shown on 'applicable sheets.' The validation methodology clarifies that existing electric utilities are typically shown on Existing Conditions or Survey sheets, while proposed electric utilities are shown on Utility Plan, Electrical Site Plan, or similar sheets. The evidence shows: (1) existing overhead electric lines are shown on Sheets 8 and 9 (Existing Conditions), properly marked and with power poles indicated; (2) proposed overhead electric lines are shown on Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan), with the appropriate line type in the legend. Both existing and proposed overhead utilities are accounted for on the appropriate sheet types, satisfying the requirement.
findings.explanation: Existing overhead electric shown on Sheets 8-9 with power poles; proposed overhead electric shown on Sheet 14 along Collier Street and Kinney Avenue
